svg.title: RMR control panel DIN-rail layout
svg.text: RMR control panel: DIN-rail layout and wiring
Sheet 1's circuits on five DIN rails with wire ducts between them. Every wire runs in a duct; the line shows its route and the terminal labels name both ends.
110 VAC compartment: separator in both ducts
Arduino Mega 2560, screw-terminal breakout on a DIN carrier
1 k from 5V to 43 and 100 nF from 40 to GND, both on the breakout
1 k from 3V3 to 20 at the Pi
to endstops X Y Z A B C,
Field cables: one twisted pair per endstop; motor cables shielded, shield to PE at the drive end.
1 X2, K2, FB1, Mega / Pi / screen bucks, PSU, K1, F0, X1, X0, PE bar
2 Star S, 0V-P bus, FB2, servo PSU (spare length at the right)
3 Drivers X Y1 Y2 Z A B C, ODrive S1, shield clamp bar
5 Field terminals X4 X5 X8 X7 X6, Pi 5, tower SSRs
Arrangement, not to scale; terminal positions are drawn where the routing is clearest.
Land each wire on the terminal it is drawn to. Measure parts before cutting rail and duct.
Gauges, copper only: mains L and N, PSU to FB1, K2, FB2 and S, S to 0V-P: 12 AWG.
F2-1 to F2-7: 18 AWG. F2-8: 16. F0 rung: 300 V insulation. Everything else: 20 AWG.
TB6600, ODrive, bucks, SSR modules, Mega and Pi need DIN clips or carriers.
Bond every rail and the frame to PE (chassis stud); 0 V meets PE only at S.
Open items and the firmware gap: sheet 1, notes 3 to 5.
Sheet 2 of 2. Legal 14 x 8.5 in, landscape. Print at 100 %.
Status: design, not yet built or tested.
